title: Definable and algebraic closure: what parameters determine

based_on.title: Model Theory — Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 27–28 (§7, definitions and Propositions 7.7–7.8; Lent 2023 lectures, notes by Leonard Tomczak)

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory

summary: Study points uniquely or finitely specified by parameters, prove the closure laws and compare elementary structures.
abstract: A formula with given parameters may pick out one point, or leave a finite list of possibilities. Definable closure collects the uniquely determined points; algebraic closure collects all points in those finite lists. We study these operations inside an arbitrary nonempty structure, prove that repeating either operation adds nothing, and show that elementary embeddings preserve the resulting closures exactly. The proof for algebraic closure must control the sizes of solution sets when their parameters vary, so we express a fixed finite bound by a first-order formula. In infinite sets with equality alone and in nonempty dense linear orders without endpoints, neither operation adds points beyond the original parameters. A two-point structure shows why unique determination is stronger than finite choice.
